claims.text: Conventionally processed single-phase ZrB2 requires temperatures above 2300 °C to develop a robust bonding network.
Earlier ZrB2 processing below 1700 °C produces incomplete bonding networks.
Earlier low-temperature ZrB2 specimens are vulnerable to oxidation and liquid plating-metal corrosion.
An SPS route using ultrafast heating, high uniaxial pressure, and a short dwell at no more than 1700 °C is the proposed intervention.
The proposed SPS route will produce near-fully densified, refined ZrB2.
A very short SPS dwell will prevent grain coarsening.
The resulting ZrB2 will have a refined, fully dense microstructure with limited porosity and optimized grain boundaries.
The refined microstructure and optimized grain boundaries will reinforce the Zr–B and B–B bonding network.
Reduced porosity and optimized grain boundaries will minimize oxidation pathways.
Ultrafast heating and high pressure promote rapid densification of ZrB2 at temperatures no higher than 1700 °C.
Ultrafast heating and high pressure cause immediate formation of strong interatomic bonds in ZrB2.
The proposed SPS route will yield well-developed, single-phase ZrB2 at substantially lower temperatures than traditional processing.
Refined grain boundaries and reduced porosity act as barriers to oxygen ingress.
Refined grain boundaries and reduced porosity act as barriers to corrosive species from liquid plating metals.
The SPS-processed ZrB2 will have mechanical strength and structural integrity comparable to conventionally sintered ZrB2 processed above 2300 °C.
The SPS-processed ZrB2 will have significantly better high-temperature oxidation resistance than both conventional high-temperature ZrB2 and earlier low-temperature specimens.
The SPS-processed ZrB2 will have significantly better liquid-metal corrosion resistance than both conventional high-temperature ZrB2 and earlier low-temperature specimens.
The resulting material is expected to remain applicable under oxidation exposure up to approximately 1500 °C and in industrial liquid plating-metal environments.
SPS at temperatures below 1700 °C has successfully produced strong, corrosion-resistant bulk material in another refractory alloy system.

contradictions.description: The predicted outcome requires mechanical strength and structural integrity merely comparable to the high-temperature baseline, whereas the falsification rule requires statistically significant improvements in mechanical properties relative to that baseline.
